rationale: Four numerical-passing, compiling observations: attempt-00 (128x64x64, st=1, sw=0) 470.78us; attempt-01 (64x128x64, st=1, sw=16) 402.23us; attempt-02 (64x128x32, st=2, sw=16) 399.54us best; attempt-03 (64x128x32, st=1, sw=16) 408.93us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB across all runs, so the analytical serpentine-reuse traffic term is NOT materializing as measured traffic; swizzle effect on latency is unconfirmed and confounded with tile/stage changes. The clearest observed lever is block_K=32 with stages=2 (attempt-02 vs attempt-03), consistent with deeper pipelining at smaller block_K. Attempt-03 regressing despite same tile as best suggests stage count matters more than swizzle. Keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] to disambiguate swizzle>0 vs swizzle=0 at matched tile/stage, and keep tile/stage domains full so HiGHS can trade tile size for extra stages under the 32KB cap (multi-stage at 64x128x32 fits; try block_M=32 to unlock stages=3). Weights: pipeline=2 (best lever observed), footprint=0.5 (actual smem pinned at hard 32KB cap in all runs so the constraint already enforces it), traffic=1 (measured DRAM flat, analytic term unreliable), launches=1 (avoid overfitting four points). Shared cap stays 32768, matching the portability cap. Next hypothesis: match tile/stage at 64x128x32/stages=2 and compare swizzle=0 vs 4 vs 8 vs 16; also probe block_M=32 with stages=3 for deeper pipelining. Validation scope: Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not run on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
